stories.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue. UKMTO said on Friday that another tanker was struck by a projectile and caught fire while outbound through the strait, extending a wave of attacks on merchant ships.
stories.why_it_matters: Hull strikes raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings, slow transits and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude, product and gas ton-miles.
stories.latest: A further tanker was hit and set on fire in the strait on Friday; separately, Banchero Costa reports Arabian Gulf crude exports down 27.6% in January-October.
sources: Tanker On Fire After Struck By Projectile Near Strait of Hormuz
Another Tanker Hit in Strait of Hormuz as Maritime Attacks Surge Worldwide
Tanker Market: Arabian Gulf Crude Oil Exports Down 27.6% This Year
Iran War Oil Premium Evaporates as Global Crude Supplies Surge

stories.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
stories.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea have continued through November, with two vessels sunk off Bulgaria and crew injured following an earlier wheat carrier capsizing.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region.
stories.latest: No direct update today; trade press notes the Russian Navy has lost ships in the Black Sea and is stretched by escort duties.
sources: Russian Navy Back in the Mediterranean Escorting a Cargo Flotilla

stories.title: Russian refining damage and diesel export limits
stories.what: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October, on top of a Russian ban on most diesel exports extended to end-January.
stories.why_it_matters: Lost Russian refining and export restrictions reshape clean product ton-miles, pulling diesel from longer-haul sources and changing MR and LR employment.

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations. The Russian Navy is now reported escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers and a cargo flotilla in the Mediterranean.
stories.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties and vessel positions, and naval escorting signals that sanctioned trades are being defended rather than curtailed.
stories.latest: Reports that the Russian Navy, stretched after Black Sea losses, is escorting sanctioned dark-fleet tankers in the Mediterranean.
sources: Russian Navy Back in the Mediterranean Escorting a Cargo Flotilla

stories.title: US-China ship fees and port state control friction
stories.what: The US has extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue, while a US congressional committee urges sanctions over China's detention of Panama-flagged ships.
stories.why_it_matters: Reinstated fees, sanctions or retaliatory detentions would change the cost and risk of deploying particular tonnage into US and Chinese trades.

stories.title: Strike threat at LA-Long Beach
stories.what: The Los Angeles-Long Beach port complex is bracing for a strike as a deadline nears, with employers warning of severe supply chain disruption if talks fail.
stories.why_it_matters: A stoppage at the largest US West Coast gateway would disrupt container flows, berth availability and inland logistics, with knock-on congestion for vessels scheduled to call.
stories.latest: More than 110 US trade associations publicly urged employers and union leaders to reach a deal as the strike deadline approaches.
sources: More Than 110 Trade Groups Urge Deal as LA-Long Beach Port Strike Deadline Nears
